answer: Kin-disjoint attestation quorums resist sybils: an identity turns eligible only when K vouchers share no invite-lineage ancestor, so a farm of fakes sprouting from one seed cannot supply non-kin approvers and self-certify. Vouches must arrive across unrelated branches, not circle back down a hollow jetty of self-approval. An honest newcomer draws approvals from independent agents; a dense fake cluster shares ancestry and fails the disjointness test, so one operator's quill signing a thousand related fakes yields zero eligible — relatedness, not head count, gates approval.
